newsitem.title: USA: Motorola quitting DRAM market, sees charge.
newsitem.headline: Motorola quitting DRAM market, sees charge.

text.p: Motorola Inc said Tuesday it will take a $170 million pre-tax charge against second quarter earnings to phase out its limited participation in the dynamic random access memory (DRAM) market.
The charges relate to the write-down of both technology development costs and manufacturing equipment, the company said.

Motorola said it has maintained a limited participation of less than five percent in the DRAM market since the mid-1980s. During the past three years, its share of the market has been less than two percent, it said.
Motorola said it expects to release its second-quarter earnings July 8. It gave no projections.

Ken Phillips, a company spokesman, said Motorola was leaving the DRAM market to redirect resources into other memory technologies, such as its proprietary Fast Static Random Access Memory, or FSRAM, and Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory, or EEPROM.
Motorola said the move will not impact employment or its long-term relationships with Toshiba Corp and Siemens AG.
Motorola said it will maintain its joint venture partnerships with both companies but, over time, will convert its share of production capacity to other products.
